fossil-springs.note: Coconino National Forest's current alerts page, rechecked directly today, confirms the Fossil Creek non-permit season (October 2 through March 31 each year) is in effect under Order #03-04-06-23-21, prohibiting camping, campfires, and glass containers in the corridor (Source: Coconino National Forest). No closure specific to Fossil Creek Trail or Fossil Springs was found. This trail crosses Fossil Creek, a tributary of the Verde River, in a canyon along the Yavapai/Gila county line. NWS Flagstaff has issued a Flood Warning for Oak Creek, West Fork Oak Creek, the Verde River, and the Sedona area, in effect until 2:00pm MST today, November 1, for flash flooding of creeks and normally dry washes that is imminent or occurring after 1.5 to 2.25 inches of rain already fell, with low-water crossings and bridges on and near SR 179 and SR 89A possibly impassable (Source: National Weather Service). The Verde River itself is forecast to crest near Camp Verde and Clarkdale under this warning, and Fossil Creek drains into the Verde downstream of those gauges, so it is marked restricted out of caution until the warning expires and conditions can be rechecked. The NWS active alerts feed for Arizona, checked directly today, shows no Excessive Heat Warning, Heat Advisory, or Red Flag Warning active anywhere in the state (Source: National Weather Service). Call the Fossil Creek hotline at 928-226-4611 for road and seasonal status before arriving, and carry extra water.

south-kaibab-ooh-aah.note: Grand Canyon National Park's Key Hiking Messages page, last updated October 27, 2026 and rechecked directly today, states South Kaibab Trail is open from the South Kaibab Trailhead to Black Bridge, which covers Ooh Aah Point and Cedar Ridge well within the open section (Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park). Black Bridge and Silver Bridge, which span the Colorado River, remain closed due to hazardous conditions caused by flash flooding, so through-hikes to Phantom Ranch or the North Rim are not possible, but South Kaibab Trail itself is open for day hikes to Ooh Aah Point and beyond. The park states there is no estimated reopening of the bridge closures at this time. Potable water is available at the South Kaibab Trailhead tank; there is no reliable water source below the trailhead. This trail is fully sun exposed. The NWS active alerts feed for Arizona, checked directly today, shows no Excessive Heat Warning, Heat Advisory, or Red Flag Warning active anywhere in the state (Source: National Weather Service).

Beyond River Resthouse, Black Bridge and Silver Bridge themselves remain closed due to hazardous conditions from flash flooding, with no estimated reopening at this time, so Phantom Ranch and the river crossing remain inaccessible. Confirm current status with the Backcountry Information Center at 928-638-7875 before descending.
